source.title: ToolEyes: Fine-Grained Evaluation for Tool Learning Capabilities of Large Language Models in Real-world Scenarios
source.authors: Junjie Ye; Guan-Yu Li; Songyang Gao; Cai-Shuang Huang; Yilong Wu; Si-Xian Li; Xiao-Ran Fan; Shi-Han Dou; Tao Ji; Qi Zhang; Tao Gui; Xuan-Jing Huang

record.file_problem: Whole paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates downstream tool-learning performance across model sizes using a benchmark, rather than measuring held-out pretraining cross-entropy or fitting scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper cites scaling-law work but does not measure held-out cross-entropy, sweep training tokens or compute, fit loss power laws, or test compute-optimal allocation. Its relevant results are tool-learning scores by scenario and overall for the size-varying LLaMA-2-chat and Vicuna-1.5 families in Table 2. Other capability-dimension scores and examples are not separate results on the downstream-performance measure used here.
record.test_reason: Section 3.4 explicitly questions improvement with model size using within-family ToolEyes results. These results bear on V6: some larger models perform substantially worse. They do not test pretraining-loss power laws or establish a quantitative downstream scaling relationship.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is substantially accurate. The authors report that tool-learning performance can weaken with increased size and attribute this to amplified conversational redundancy and escaped-character errors. They also explicitly state that core abilities improve with size, including better answer organization for LLaMA-2-chat-13B. Their proposed explanations are observational interpretations rather than controlled causal findings.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates tool-use benchmark scores rather than held-out pretraining loss; no power-law fitting, extrapolation, or compute-allocation sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model size and scenario. Open-source models use five-shot prompts while other models use zero-shot prompts; inference uses temperature 0.3 and top_p 0.5, and some scores are judged by GPT-4.
record.problems: The results measure tool-learning benchmark performance, not general downstream performance or pretraining loss. Size comparisons cover only a few models in two families, without controlled re-training of a single model configuration across sizes. The study reports no uncertainty estimates for the Table 2 scores, although it reports ANOVA p-values for scenario differences.
record.rows_left_out: No Table 2 results for models without a within-family size comparison were retained. The other listed models do not form a parameter-size series in this evaluation. Figure 5 and the appendices' individual capability scores were not extracted as separate downstream-performance rows.

untested.parts: Held-out pretraining loss and power-law dependence on parameters, tokens, or compute.
Extrapolating larger-run loss from small-run fits.
Architecture variation at fixed parameter count.
Power-law form in other modalities or training regimes; evaluating fine-tuned models alone does not test this form.
Quantitative prediction from fitted scaling relationships, dependence on pretraining loss, and generalization beyond the tested tool-learning benchmark.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits on setup and fitting choices, and departures from single power laws.

record.verdict_notes: All Table 2 values are correctly transcribed. Scores are averages of five capability dimensions, not task-success percentages. Within-family comparisons use five-shot ReAct prompts, a nine-turn limit, temperature 0.3, and top_p 0.5. Model training differences are not controlled, no scaling relationship is fitted, and no uncertainty is reported for these size comparisons. Table 3 tests scenario differences, not size effects. These findings concern V6 in this evaluation setting and do not challenge V1 or establish V7.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of larger-run loss from fits on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Power-law behavior in other modalities or training regimes.

Only tool-learning benchmark performance across selected model sizes is tested; the study does not relate downstream performance to pretraining loss or establish a general relationship across downstream tasks.
The paper does not fit loss-scaling exponents or compare choices for parameter counting, training schedule, data, or fitting method.
